summary: This work extends spectator-qubit noise mitigation from two-level random-telegraph noise to general $L$-level fluctuator processes by developing a map-based formalism with $L \times L$ matrices and deriving a heuristic adaptive protocol that dynamically selects measurement angle $\theta_n$ and waiting time $\tau_n$ based on current noise estimates. Numerical simulations for $L=3$ show decoherence rates of $\sim 10^{-9}$ under the adaptive strategy, achieving comparable suppression to the two-level case despite noise complexity.
motivation: Realistic solid-state environments feature multiple charge traps and defects causing complex multi-level noise rather than simple two-level random-telegraph processes, making noise-mitigation strategies that handle general fluctuator spectra essential for practical quantum systems.
method: The authors generalize the Bayesian map-based formalism to arbitrary $L$ noise levels described by transition rates $\gamma_{ij}$ and formulate the problem in terms of accumulated noise-time vectors $\bar{X}$. A heuristic adaptive algorithm identifies the two most-likely noise levels $\mu$ and $\nu$ from the coherence vector $\bar{A}_n$, then selects $\tau_{n+1} = \pi/|K_\mu - K_\nu|$ and $\theta_{n+1}$ to maximally distinguish these hypotheses.
result: For $L=3$ with transition rates $\gamma_{12}=0.1$ to $\gamma_{32}=0.3$ and sensitivities $\kappa_i \in [0.001, 0.005]$, $K_i \in [40, 180]$, the adaptive algorithm suppresses the decoherence rate to $(9.5\text{--}9.6) \times 10^{-10}$ compared to uncontrolled decay, with performance bounded by a conservative upper bound scaling as $\Gamma^\mathrm{ub} \propto \gamma(\Delta\kappa/\Delta K)^2$.
